sample_unit: patient MRI sequences from five external institutions (plus 30 patients at INST1 post-deployment)

links.outcome: Change in segmentation performance over time at the same institution after acquisition protocol change
links.effect: Whole gland DSC fell from 99.46±0.12% to 91.24±3.32% (P<.001); RVD changed from -0.006±0.127% to 8.10±8.16% (P<.001) after protocol change at INST1.
links.quote: The model presented a significant degradation for the whole gland (WG) in the presence of a change of acquisition protocol at INST1 (DSC:99.46±0.12% and 91.24±3.32%, P <.001; RVD:-0.006±0.127% and 8.10±8.16%, P <.001).

links.outcome: Segmentation performance across external institutions with different scanners and PI-RADS adherence
links.effect: Higher performance in PI-RADS v2.1-adherent centers than non-adherent (DSC 86.24±9.67% vs 74.83±15.45%, P<.001; RVD -6.50±18.46% vs 1.64±29.12%, P=.003).
links.quote: The model had a significantly higher performance in centers adhering to PI-RADS v2.1 when compared to those that did not (DSC: 86.24±9.67% and 74.83±15.45%, P <.001; RVD: -6.50±18.46% and 1.64±29.12%, P =.003).

unlisted_practices: Adhering to PI-RADS v2.1 technical acquisition standards to improve inter-institutional transferability of imaging AI

screen.reason: The study empirically tests how adherence to imaging acquisition standards (PI-RADS v2.1) and post-deployment protocol changes impact model degradation and multi-center transferability.

primary.practice: adherence to technical imaging standards (PI-RADS v2.1) and protocol drift monitoring
